candidates.title: The Ancient Art of Smoking Food
candidates.opening: Around 780,000 years ago at a site in what is now Israel, early humans hung elephant meat over smoky fires. They weren't just cooking dinner—they were inventing one of humanity's oldest food preservation techniques. Smoking food means exposing meats, fish, or vegetables to smoke from burning wood. candidates.title: The Rocket Company That Almost Ran Out of Money
candidates.opening: In September 2008, a small rocket called Falcon 1 sat on a launch pad on Kwajalein Atoll in the Pacific Ocean. Three launches had already failed. The company, SpaceX, had only enough money left for one more try. If this rocket failed too, the company would close. Elon Musk had started SpaceX in 2002 with a big dream: cheaper rockets that could someday carry people to Mars.

No leader calls out directions, yet the entire group moves like a single living creature. This amazing display is called collective animal behavior. candidates.title: The Book That Opened Up Machines
candidates.opening: One page explains how a ball-point pen works. A few hundred pages later, another explains a nuclear reactor. Both appear in the same book, and both are written so that a curious kid can follow along. The book is called How Things Work: The Universal Encyclopedia of Machines. It was written for people with no special training who still wanted to know what was happening inside the machines around them.

Byzantine letters and Ottoman court records still survive, and historians compare them to work out what happened, and when. History is the study of past human events, pieced together from evidence like old letters, records and objects.
